title: Characterization of the fast neutron response of liquid scintillator detectors at NFS
byline: Fiol; A Pérez de Rada; Del Río; G; Martínez; T; Ledoux; X; Alcayne; Ballesteros; Cano-Ott; Matea; I; Miriot-Jaubert; Plaza; Sánchez-Caballero; Vandebrouck; Vill
html:
Abstract:The fast neutron response of MONSTER and sTED liquid scintillation detectors was investigated using time-of-flight measurements at the Neutrons For Science facility at GANIL-SPIRAL2. A continuous neutron beam produced by 40 MeV deuterons on a thick beryllium converter was used to obtain pulse height distributions for selected incident neutron energies. Digital pulse shape analysis was used to distinguish neutron-induced events and reduce pile-up effects. For MONSTER, the response and detection efficiency were studied up to 40 MeV using Geant4 with previously obtained light output functions and PHITS in SCINFUL mode. The comparison examines the increasing importance of carbon reaction channels and the divergence between the calculated efficiencies above 20 MeV. For sTED, light output functions for recoil deuterons and alpha particles were determined for the first time for this detector. The measured and calculated efficiencies were compared up to 20 MeV. The sTED efficiency shows a good overall agreement with the simulations. These results provide experimentally constrained detector response information for nuclear data measurements and identify limitations that must be considered when extending the simulations to higher neutron energies.
